question: In SQL, what is the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
answer: In SQL, the WHERE clause filters individual rows before any grouping occurs, as stated in [S1] and [S1]. On the other hand, the HAVING clause filters whole groups after aggregation, as defined in [S1] and [S1] [S2]. provides information about NULL in SQL, unrelated to WHERE and HAVING.

S3.text:
1. Selecting Rows and Columns
In pandas, df.loc selects by label and df.iloc selects by integer position. A label slice such as
df.loc['a':'c'] includes the end label 'c', whereas a position slice such as df.iloc[0:3] excludes position
3.
Boolean masks such as df[df['amount'] > 100] keep the rows where the condition is true.
df.query('amount > 100') expresses the same filter as a string.

S4.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S4.text: 4. Sampling and Confidence Intervals A population is the entire group of interest and a sample is a subset used to learn about it. Simple random sampling gives every member an equal chance of selection; stratified sampling samples within subgroups; convenience sampling is easy but prone to bias. Sampling bias occurs when the sample systematically differs from the population. The sampling distribution of the mean describes how sample means vary from sample to sample. The Central Limit Theorem states that for sufficiently large n the distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal with mean mu and standard error sigma / sqrt(n), regardless of the shape of the original population. S6.title: Data Wrangling Handbook
S6.text:
2. Missing Values
pandas represents missing numbers as NaN. isna() flags them, dropna() removes rows with any
missing value by default, and fillna(value) replaces them. NaN is not equal to itself, so a
comparison such as x == np.nan is never true; use isna() instead.
In SQL the missing marker is NULL, and a comparison with NULL is unknown, so use IS NULL
rather than = NULL. Aggregations such as AVG ignore NULL values; the pandas mean() skips
NaN by default (skipna=True).
